skills.name: awareness
skills.summary: Show cross-repo awareness: peer view (who's working on what in this repo) and org-wide progress (Product Roadmap). Renders both views by default.
triggers: who else is working on this

skills.name: build
skills.summary: Build a feature from start to finish — plans the work, executes it, and verifies the result in one command.
notes: Use when the user wants to build something, implement a feature, or work on an objective end-to-end.

skills.name: cleanup
skills.summary: Archive old objective directories from completed milestones to reduce clutter.
notes: Moves completed work to the milestones archive — use only when explicitly requested.

skills.name: debug
skills.summary: Investigate bugs using a structured approach that survives context resets. Tracks hypotheses, evidence, and progress across sessions.
notes: Use when the user reports a bug, error, or something not working as expected.

skills.name: decide
skills.summary: Resolve a parked decision and resume autonomous execution.
notes: Use when you see a pending DECISION-NNN.md in .planning/decisions/pending/, when the user wants to choose an option for a blocked checkpoint:decision, or when you need to tell the executor which option to take.

skills.name: design-review
skills.summary: Run the ADVISORY UI design-critique sweep on a Flutter surface or objective: capture (or reuse) each declared UI state, critique it against the project design system through the design-critic engine, and present a prioritized design-debt list.
notes: This is advisory design critique — it NEVER gates. The heavy first-run produces a ranked design-debt backlog whose high-priority items feed the objective-work loop.
Use when the user wants a design review, design critique, polish pass, or design-debt audit of a UI surface.

skills.name: discuss-objective
skills.summary: Capture implementation decisions for an objective before planning — lock in preferences so research and planning don't drift into assumptions.
notes: Use when the user wants to shape how an objective gets built before tasks are generated.
triggers: before planning I want to discuss

skills.name: execute-objective
skills.summary: Execute all planned tasks for an objective, running independent tasks in parallel for speed.
notes: Use when the user wants to run or execute an already-planned objective.

skills.name: flow
skills.summary: Orchestrate a multi-step DevFlow workflow by chaining skills. Use when the user wants to invoke a sequence of skills as one ask (e.g., "build and sync to github", "research, plan, then build", "ship and announce").

skills.name: gh-sync
skills.summary: Sync DevFlow planning state to GitHub — create/update objective issues, generate release notes, or push a single objective's state (body + sticky comment + Project v2 fields).

skills.name: handoff
skills.summary: Hand off a TTY-required or shell-env-dependent command to the user's shell.
notes: Use for auth flows (gh auth login, doctl auth init, npm login) or shell-init commands (nvm/mise/conda activate, direnv). Non-disruptive when devflow-watch is running.
skills.args: <command to run interactively or via user shell>

skills.name: help
skills.summary: Show available DevFlow commands and usage guide.
notes: Use when the user asks about DevFlow capabilities, available commands, or how to use the system.

skills.name: initiatives
skills.summary: Manage strategic initiative context — sync GitHub Epics to disk, list cached initiatives, or show a single initiative body. Planner reads these at plan time.

skills.name: list-objective-assumptions
skills.summary: See what Claude plans to do for an objective before it starts, so you can course-correct early.
notes: Shows the intended approach without creating any files.

skills.name: map-codebase
skills.summary: Analyze an existing codebase to understand its stack, architecture, conventions, and concerns before starting new work.
notes: Use when the user wants to understand, analyze, or map an existing codebase.
triggers: what does this codebase look like?
skills.args: [optional: specific area to map, e.g., 'api' or 'auth']

skills.name: micro
skills.summary: Sub-30-LOC, single-file changes. The cheapest DevFlow path (~2k tokens). Use for typo fixes, single-line bug fixes, prop renames, dependency bumps, missing semicolons.

skills.name: milestone
skills.summary: Manage milestones: start a new one, audit a finished one, complete it, or plan gap-closure objectives.
notes: Subcommand-style: /devflow:milestone new | audit | complete | gaps
Use when explicitly requested.

skills.name: new-project
skills.summary: Set up a new project from scratch — asks what you're building, researches the domain, defines requirements, and creates a development roadmap.
notes: Use when the user wants to start a new project or initialize DevFlow for the first time.

skills.name: objective
skills.summary: Add or remove an objective from the current milestone roadmap.
notes: Subcommand-style: /devflow:objective add | remove
Use when explicitly requested.
Note: 'insert' (decimal objectives) was removed in v1.2 — use 'add' instead.

skills.name: plan-objective
skills.summary: Create a detailed execution plan for an objective, breaking it into concrete tasks with success criteria.
notes: Use when the user wants to plan an objective, create execution plans, or prepare for building.

skills.name: quick
skills.summary: Small features (single executor, no planner, no verifier) — between micro (1-line) and build (multi-subsystem). Cutoff: <5 files, <200 LOC, no new abstractions.
notes: Use when the change is too big for /devflow:micro but doesn't warrant full /devflow:build planning.

skills.name: research-objective
skills.summary: Research how to build something before planning it — discovers best practices, architecture patterns, and pitfalls for the domain.
notes: Use when the user wants to investigate, research, or explore options before planning an objective.
triggers: what's the best approach for objective

skills.name: security-audit
skills.summary: Scan the codebase for security vulnerabilities — checks for secrets, auth flaws, dependency risks, and OWASP Top 10 issues.
notes: Standalone — works without project setup. Covers secrets, auth, dependencies, and code-level vulnerabilities.
skills.args: [optional: path scope like 'src/api' or focus filter like 'secrets-only', 'auth-only', 'deps-only']

skills.name: set-profile
skills.summary: Switch between quality, balanced, and budget model profiles to control cost and capability.
notes: Use when the user wants to change the AI model tier for DevFlow agents.

skills.name: settings
skills.summary: Configure which agents run, which AI models they use, and how the workflow behaves.
notes: Use when the user wants to change DevFlow settings or configure workflow behavior.

skills.name: status
skills.summary: Consolidated status/resume/pause/health — `/devflow:status [resume|pause|check]`.
notes: Default: show progress + route to next action. Subcommands: check (integrity), pause (save context), resume (restore context). Both flag and bare forms accepted.
triggers: pick up where we left off

skills.name: sync-roadmap
skills.summary: Reconcile ROADMAP.md checkbox state against on-disk SUMMARY.md presence. Default: silently corrects drift; --dry-run previews; --interactive prompts per change.

skills.name: todo
skills.summary: Manage todos: capture an idea/task or view the morning standup across local + GitHub + peer sources.
notes: Subcommand-style: /devflow:todo add | list
Use when the user wants to save something for later, note an idea, or get a "what should I work on?" view.

skills.name: tui
skills.summary: Open the program-aware TUI viewer — read-only terminal UI showing parallel sessions, org tree, and active initiatives in three stacked panels. tmux-safe; reflows narrow terminals.

skills.name: ui-eval
skills.summary: Run the UI visual-evaluation pipeline on a Flutter surface or objective: capture each declared UI state and score it. Default (no --judge, or --judge labels) is an ADVISORY offline label-echo lookup (no network, no real vision comparison) — it can never clear a surface from human verification. Only --judge live (a real Anthropic vision call) produces a BINDING gate.
notes: Use when the user wants to visually evaluate, judge, or dogfood a UI surface's rendered states.

skills.name: verify-work
skills.summary: Test what was built by walking through expected behavior and checking it matches reality.
notes: Use when the user wants to test, verify, or validate what was built in an objective.

skills.name: workstreams
skills.summary: Run independent objectives in parallel using git worktrees, then merge results back.
notes: Subcommand-style: /devflow:workstreams setup | status | merge | run
Advanced parallel execution — use only when explicitly requested.

agents.name: codebase-mapper
agents.description: Analyzes a codebase from a specific angle (stack, architecture, quality, or concerns) and writes structured findings.

agents.name: debugger
agents.description: Investigates bugs using a structured scientific method with persistent session state across context resets.

agents.name: executor
agents.description: Executes planned tasks with atomic git commits, handles deviations, and manages checkpoints during builds.

agents.name: integration-checker
agents.description: Verifies that separately-built features connect properly and end-to-end user workflows actually work.

agents.name: job-checker
agents.description: Reviews execution plans before they run to verify they will actually achieve the objective goal.

agents.name: objective-researcher
agents.description: Researches how to implement an objective — discovers best practices, patterns, and pitfalls before planning begins.

agents.name: planner
agents.description: Creates detailed execution plans for objectives with task breakdown, dependency ordering, and built-in quality checks.

agents.name: project-researcher
agents.description: Researches the domain ecosystem for a new project — stack options, architecture patterns, features, and common pitfalls.

agents.name: research-synthesizer
agents.description: Combines findings from multiple parallel research agents into a unified summary for roadmap creation.

agents.name: roadmapper
agents.description: Creates project roadmaps by breaking requirements into ordered objectives with success criteria and dependency mapping.

agents.name: security-auditor
agents.description: Scans codebase for security vulnerabilities in a specific domain: secrets, auth flows, or dependency risks.

agents.name: ui-evaluator
agents.description: Machine-judges the visual correctness of Flutter UI states by capturing each declared surface, scoring it through the offline visual-eval engine, and writing evidence the verifier consumes.

agents.name: verifier
agents.description: Verifies that built code actually achieves the objective goal, not just that tasks were completed.

hooks.name: awareness-cache-populate
hooks.purpose: Warms the cross-repo awareness cache in a detached child process. Never blocks session start, even when a scan takes 30s or more.

hooks.name: changelog-on-tag
hooks.purpose: Blocks `git tag -a vX.Y.Z` unless CHANGELOG.md has a `## [X.Y.Z]` heading and the three release manifests carry matching versions.

hooks.name: classify-session
hooks.purpose: Classifies the project as `ambient`, `init-offer`, or `skip` and injects the routing decision table you see at session start.

hooks.name: gate-commits
hooks.purpose: Blocks raw `git commit` and redirects to `df-tools commit`, which preserves objective scope and task IDs and updates STATE.md. Detection is invocation-aware: heredoc bodies and quoted arguments are stripped first, so prose that merely mentions the command is not gated.

hooks.name: gate-edits
hooks.purpose: Strict DENY by default in ambient mode. Allows edits when a live `.planning/.skill-active` marker exists (resolved from both the local and the main checkout, so worktree-isolated agents are not denied by a marker they cannot see), when the prompt carries an override phrase, or when the env escape is set. Targets outside the project root are never gated. Severity is per-project via `gates.editGate`.

hooks.name: gate-interactive
hooks.purpose: Intercepts TTY-requiring commands and routes them to the handoff watcher rather than letting them hang on a prompt no one can answer.

hooks.name: guard-no-progress
hooks.purpose: Detects the same tool being called with identical arguments repeatedly: warns at 3, escalates to `ask` at 5, and resets whenever the agent varies its approach. Step limits cannot catch a stuck loop — they only fire once the whole budget is spent.

hooks.name: inject-handoff-results
hooks.purpose: Surfaces completed handoff-watcher results back into the session.

hooks.name: inject-org-context
hooks.purpose: Injects an objective’s full org context — parent issue, repo roadmap, sibling repo activity — at planning time.

hooks.name: route-intent
hooks.purpose: Matches the prompt against build/plan/verify/debug intent and injects a directive to route through the matching skill instead of editing code directly. Regexes require imperative form, so plain questions do not trip it.

hooks.name: route-results
hooks.purpose: Injects completed handoff-watcher results into the next turn, so a queued interactive command resumes without you pasting anything.

hooks.name: statusline
hooks.purpose: Renders model, current task, directory, and context usage in the Claude Code status line.

hooks.name: sync-runtime
hooks.purpose: Mirrors the plugin-bundled runtime to `~/.claude/devflow/` whenever the bundled version differs from the cached `.plugin-version`. Skills reference `@~/.claude/devflow/...` paths, which do not interpolate `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` — this hook is what makes those references resolve.

hooks.name: verify-commits
hooks.purpose: Warns when a subagent finishes without producing commits — a silent-failure detector for the executor.

hooks.name: verify-completion
hooks.purpose: Checks that the most recent SUMMARY.md carries task evidence and no failure markers. Warns only — never blocks.
